76:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Insan It was mentioned in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite in the dawn prayer on Friday, “Alif, Lam, Meem. The revelation” al-Sajdah and Has there not been over man a period of time? Abdullah ibn Wahb said: Ibn Zayd told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this surah, Has there not been over man a period of time? and it was revealed to him and there was a black man with him. When he reached the description of Paradise, he sighed and his soul left him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The soul of your companion - or he said your brother - has left him - is the longing for Paradise. A strange mursal. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God the Almighty says, informing us about man, that He created him after he was nothing worth mentioning due to his insignificance and weakness. God the Almighty said: Has there not been over man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning? Then He explained that, saying, Indeed, We created man from a mixed sperm-drop, meaning mixtures. Mixture and mingling are things that are mixed together. Ibn Abbas said about God the Almighty’s statement: from a mixed sperm-drop, meaning the man’s semen and the woman’s semen when they come together and mix, then it moves from one stage to another, one state to another, and one color to another. This is what Ikrimah, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: Mixture is the mixing of the man’s semen with the woman’s semen. And the Almighty’s saying: We will test him means that We will examine him, as the Almighty said: To test you, which of you is best in deed. “And We made him hearing and seeing” means that We gave him hearing and sight, with which he could perform acts of obedience and disobedience. God the Almighty said: {Indeed, We showed him the way} meaning, We made it clear to him, explained it to him, and gave him insight into it, just as God the Almighty said: {And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness to guidance}. And His statement the Almighty said: {And We showed him the two ways}, meaning, We showed him the path of good and the path of evil. This is the well-known opinion of Ikrimah, Atiyah, Ibn Zayd, and Mujahid, and the majority of scholars. It was narrated from Mujahid, Abu Salih, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi that they said regarding God the Almighty’s statement: {Indeed, We showed him the way}, meaning his emergence from the womb. This is a strange opinion, but the correct and well-known one is the first one. God the Almighty said: {Either grateful or ungrateful}, in the accusative case as a state of the ha’ in His statement: {Indeed, We showed him the way}, meaning he is either miserable or happy in that, as came in the hadith narrated by Muslim on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Ash’ari, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Everyone sets out in the morning, selling his soul, either ruining it or freeing it. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Khathim, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ka’b ibn Ujrah, May God protect you from the leadership of fools. He said, And what is the leadership of fools? He said, “Leaders who will come after me who are not guided by my guidance, nor do they follow my Sunnah. Whoever believes their lies and helps them in their injustice, then they are not of me, and I am not of them, and they will not come to my Cistern. Whoever does not believe their lies and does not help them in their injustice, then they are of me, and I am of them, and they will come to my Cistern. O Ka’b ibn Ujrah, fasting is a shield, and charity extinguishes sin, and prayer brings one closer to God—or he said, proof—O Ka’b ibn Ujrah, flesh that grows from ill-gotten gains will not enter Paradise; the Fire is more deserving of it. O Ka’b, people go out in the morning and evening. The one who buys his soul frees it, and the one who sells his soul destroys it.” And it was narrated on the authority of Ghiyath ibn Wahb, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khathim, with this chain of transmission. It was mentioned in Surat Ar-Rum, when God Almighty said, The fitrah of God upon which He created mankind, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every child is born in a state of fitrah until his tongue expresses it. When his tongue expresses it, he is either grateful or ungrateful.” Imam Ahmad said: Abu Amir told us, Abdullah bin Jaafar told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Muhammad, on the authority of Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “No one goes out except that at his door are two banners: a banner in the hand of an angel and a banner in the hand of a devil. If he goes out for what God loves, the angel will follow him with his banner, and he will remain under the king’s banner until he returns to his home. But if he goes out for what God is displeased with, the devil will follow him with his banner, and he will remain under the devil’s banner until he returns to his home.”

76:4: God Almighty tells us about what He has prepared for the unbelievers of His creation in terms of chains, shackles, and the Blaze, which is the flame and burning in the fire of Hell, as God Almighty says: When the shackles are around their necks and the chains, they will be dragged * In the scalding water, then in the Fire they will be blazing. And when He mentioned what He has prepared for these wretched ones of the Blaze, He said after that: Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is of camphor. And He knows what camphor has in terms of cooling and pleasant smell, along with what is added to that of pleasure in Paradise. Al-Hasan said: The coolness of the camphor is in the fragrance of the ginger. That is why He said: A spring from which the servants of God will drink, making it gush forth abundantly. That is, what was mixed of camphor for these righteous people is a spring from which the close servants of God will drink purely without mixing and they will be quenched with their thirst. That is why He included the meaning of is quenched even if He made it transitive with the preposition bi and placed ayn in the accusative case as a specification. Some of them said: This drink is like camphor in its fragrance. Some of them said: It is from the spring of camphor. Some of them said: It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case with is drunk. Ibn Jarir narrated these three sayings. God the Almighty said: is made to gush forth abundantly meaning they will dispose of it as they wish and wherever they wish in their palaces, homes, gatherings and shops. Gushing forth means flowing as God the Almighty said: And they said, ‘We will not believe in you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth.’ And He said: And We caused a river to gush forth within them. Mujahid said: They blow it up means they drive it wherever they want. This is what Ikrimah and Qatadah said. Ath-Thawri said: They divert it wherever they want. God’s statement: They fulfill their vows and fear a Day whose evil will be widespread means they worship God through what He has enjoined upon them of performing the obligatory acts of worship based on the original Shari’ah and what they have enjoined upon themselves through vows. Imam Malik narrated from Talhah ibn Abd al-Malik al-Ayli from al-Qasim ibn Malik from Aisha may God be pleased with her that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Whoever vows to obey God, let him obey Him, and whoever vows to disobey God, let him not disobey Him. Narrated by al-Bukhari from the hadith of Malik. And they abandon the forbidden things that He forbade them from, fearing the evil of the Day of Judgment, which is the day whose evil will spread widely among the people, except for those upon whom God has mercy. Ibn Abbas said: Widespread. Qatada said: By God, the evil of that day will spread until it fills the heavens and the earth. Ibn Jarir said: “From this is their saying: The crack in the bottle spread and became long.” From this is the saying of Al-A’sha: Then she appeared, and she had caused a great deal of harm to my heart, a rift that had spread over her absence. Meaning widespread. And the saying of God the Almighty: {And they give food in spite of their love for it} It was said about the love of God the Almighty, and they made the pronoun refer to God the Almighty because the context indicates it, and it is more apparent that the pronoun refers to the food, meaning they give food in a state of their love and desire for it, as Mujahid and Muqatil said, and Ibn Jarir chose it like the saying of God the Almighty: {And gives wealth in spite of its love} and the saying of God the Almighty: {You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love}. Al-Bayhaqi narrated through the path of Al-A’mash from Nafi’ who said: Ibn ‘Umar fell ill and desired grapes. The first thing the grapes brought was a desire for grapes, so Safiyyah, meaning his wife, sent and bought a bunch of grapes for a dirham, and a beggar followed the messenger, and when he entered with him the beggar said: The beggar. Ibn ‘Umar said: Give it to him. So they gave it to him. Then she sent another dirham and bought a bunch of grapes, and the messenger followed the beggar, and when he entered the beggar said: The beggar. Ibn Omar said: Give it to him. So they gave it to him. Safiyya sent word to the beggar and said: By God, if you come back, you will never get any good from him again. Then she sent another dirham and bought it with it. In Sahih Muslim, it is stated: The best charity is to give charity while you are healthy and stingy, hoping for wealth and fearing poverty. That is, while you love money, are keen on it, and are in need of it. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And they give food, in spite of their love for it, to the poor, the orphan, and the captive. As for the poor and the orphan, their description and explanation have already been given. As for the captive, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, and al-Dahhak said: The captive is from the people of the Qiblah. Ibn Abbas said: Their captives at that time were polytheists. This is supported by the fact that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) ordered his companions on the day of Badr to honor the captives, so they would give them precedence over themselves at lunch. Ikrimah said: They are the slaves. Ibn Jarir chose this because the verse is general for both Muslims and polytheists. Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Ata’, al-Hasan, and Qatadah said the same. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recommended kindness to slaves in more than one hadith, and the last thing he recommended was: Prayer and those whom your right hands possess. Mujahid said: He is the one who is imprisoned, meaning they feed these people food even though they desire it. They love Him, saying in their hearts, We feed you only for the sake of God, meaning in the hope of God’s reward and pleasure. We do not want from you any reward or thanks, meaning we do not ask you to reward us with it, nor for you to thank us before people. Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair said: By God, they did not say it with their tongues, but God knew of it in their hearts, so He praised them for it. So that someone might desire it. Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day of frowning and distress. That is, we only do this so that God may have mercy on us and meet us with His kindness on the Day of Frowning and Displeasure. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Frowning means narrow, Frowning means long. Ikrimah and others said on his authority regarding the statement, A Day of Frowning and Displeasure, that the disbeliever will frown on that day until sweat like tar will flow from between his eyes. Mujahid said, Frowning means the one with frowning lips. Frowning means the face will be tightened with pus. Saeed bin Jubair and Qatadah said: Faces will frown on it from terror. Frowning means the constriction of the forehead and between the eyes from terror. Ibn Zayd said: Al-Abous is evil, and Al-Qamatarir is severe. The clearest, most evident, sweetest, highest and most deserving expressions are the words of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qamatarir is severe. It is said: It is a Qamatarir day, a Qamatar day, a difficult day and a difficult day. It has rained today, it rains heavily, and that is the most severe and longest day in affliction and hardship. From this, some of them said: Our cousins, do you remember our affliction? If it was a day of calamities, God the Almighty said: So God will save them from the evil of that Day and will meet them with radiance and joy. This is a clear example of similarity. So God will save them from the evil of that Day means He will make them safe from what they feared. And will meet them with radiance meaning in their faces. And joy meaning in their hearts. This was said by Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Qatadah, Abu Al-Aaliyah, and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas. This is like His statement: Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, laughing and rejoicing. This is because when the heart is happy, the face will light up. Ka’b bin Malik said in his lengthy hadith. When the face of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was happy, it would be like a split moon. Aisha may God be pleased with her said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered upon me happy, his face beaming with joy. The statement of God the Almighty: And He rewarded them for what they patiently endured means because of their patience, He gave them, bestowed upon them, and housed them in Paradise and silk, meaning a spacious home, a comfortable life, and fine clothing. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated in the biography of Hisham bin Sulayman al-Darani, saying: Surah Has there come upon man a period of time? was recited to Abu Sulayman al-Darani. When the reciter reached the verse: And He rewarded them for what they patiently endured with a garden and silk garments, he said: For what they patiently endured in abandoning desires in this world. Then he recited: How many are killed by lust and how many are captured? Shame on a desire other than what is beautiful. Man's desires bring him humiliation and lead him to long-term misery.

76:13: God Almighty tells us about the people of Paradise and the eternal bliss they will enjoy therein and the abundant grace He has bestowed upon them. God Almighty says: Reclining therein on couches. We have already discussed this in Surat As-Saffat, and mentioned the disagreement over reclining, whether it means lying down, sitting cross-legged, or sitting comfortably, and that the couches are the beds under the curtains. And the Almighty said: They will see therein neither sun nor freezing cold, meaning they will not have a disturbing heat nor a painful cold, rather it is a single, permanent, everlasting temperate climate, and they do not desire a change from it. And its shades will be brought low to them, meaning its branches will be close to them. And its fruits will be made accessible, meaning whenever someone approaches it, the fruits will be brought close to him and will hang from the top of its branch as if it were listening and obedient, as the Almighty said in the other verse: And the fruits of the two gardens will be within reach. And the Almighty said: And its fruits will be within reach. Mujahid said: And its fruits will be made accessible, if he stands, they will rise with him a certain amount, and if he sits, they will be made accessible to him until he reaches them, and if he lies down, they will be made accessible to him until he reaches them. This is what the Almighty said: accessible. Qatadah said: Neither thorns nor distance will hold their hands away from it. Mujahid said: The land of Paradise is made of leaves, its soil is made of musk, the roots of its trees are made of gold and silver, and its branches are made of fresh pearls, emeralds, and rubies, and the leaves and fruits are between that. Whoever eats it while standing, it will not harm him. Whoever eats it while sitting, it will not harm him. Whoever eats it while lying down, it will not harm him. And His statement, may His Majesty be glorified: And there will be served to them vessels of silver and cups meaning that servants will serve to them with food vessels, which are made of silver, and drinking cups, which are cups that have no handles or spouts. And His statement, Vessels, vessels of silver the first is accusative as the predicate of was meaning they were vessels, and the second is accusative either as a substitute or as a distinction because He, may He be glorified and exalted, made it clear with His statement, may He be glorified and exalted: Vessels of silver Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others said: The whiteness of silver is in the clarity of glass, and the cups are only made of glass. So these cups are made of silver, and yet they are transparent, so that what is inside them can be seen from what is outside. This is something that has no equal in this world. Ibn Al-Mubarak said, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: There is nothing in Paradise but that you have been given something similar to it in this world, except for cups of silver. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. And the statement of God, "Measure them with [a precise] estimate" means according to their watering place, neither more nor less, rather they are prepared for that, measured according to the watering place of their owner. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Abu Salih, Qatadah, Ibn Abi Zayd, Abdullah bin Ubaidullah bin Umair, Al-Sha'bi and Ibn Zayd. Ibn Jarir and others also said it. This expresses the care, honor and dignity. Al-Awfi said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, "Measure them with [a precise] estimate" means it was measured for the palm of the hand. Ar-Rabi' bin Anas said the same, and Ad-Dahhak said, according to the size of the hand of the servant. This does not contradict the first statement, for they are measured in measure and watering place. And the Almighty’s saying: And they will be given to drink therein a cup whose mixture is of ginger means that they will also be given to drink, meaning the righteous, in these cups a cup meaning wine whose mixture is of ginger. Sometimes the drink is mixed for them with camphor while it is cold, and sometimes with ginger while it is hot, so that the matter is balanced. These people will have a mixture of this and that sometimes, but as for those brought near, they will drink from each of them pure, as Qatadah and others have said. And the Almighty’s saying, A spring from which the servants of God will drink has already been mentioned, and He said here: A spring therein called Salsabil meaning ginger, a spring in Paradise called Salsabil. Ikrimah said: It is the name of a spring in Paradise. Mujahid said: It was named thus because of the smoothness of its flow and the intensity of its running. Qatadah said: A spring therein called Salsabil is a smooth spring whose water is derived. Ibn Jarir narrated from some of them that it was named thus because of its smoothness in the throat, and he chose that it includes all of that, and it is as he said. God the Almighty says: {And there will circulate among them immortal youths. When you see them, you will think them to be scattered pearls.} That is, there will circulate among the people of Paradise to serve them. {Immortal} youths, that is, they will remain in one state, forever, never changing from it, and their lives will not exceed that age. Whoever interprets them as having earrings in their ears only expressed the meaning in that way, because that is more appropriate for the young, not the old. God the Almighty says: {When you see them, you will think them to be scattered pearls.} That is, when you see them spread out to attend to the needs of the masters, and their great numbers, and the beauty of their faces, and the beauty of their colors, and their clothes, and their jewelry, you will think them to be scattered pearls. There is no better comparison than this, and no better sight than pearls scattered in a beautiful place. Qatadah said, on the authority of Abu Ayyub, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr: There is no one among the people of Paradise except that a thousand servants strive for him, each servant doing the same work as his companion. And the Almighty said: And when you see meaning, and if you see, O Muhammad, then meaning there, meaning in Paradise and its delights, spaciousness, elevation, and what is in it of joy and happiness you will see delights and a great kingdom meaning, a kingdom of God there, great and dazzling, and a dazzling authority. It is proven in the Sahih that God Almighty will say to the last of the people of Hell to leave it and the last of the people of Paradise to enter it: You will have the equivalent of this world and ten times as much. We have already mentioned in the hadith narrated by Thawir ibn Abi Fakhita on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The lowest in status in Paradise is he who looks at his kingdom for a distance of a thousand years, looking at its farthest part as he looks at its nearest part. He said: ‘O Messenger of God, you have been favored over us with images, colors, and prophethood. Tell me, if I believe in what you believe in and act according to what I have acted, will I be with you in Paradise?’ He said: ‘Yes, by the One in Whose hand is my soul, the whiteness of black can be seen in Paradise from a distance of a thousand years.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever says there is no god but God has a covenant with God about it, and whoever says…’ Glory be to God and praise be to Him. He has been credited with one hundred thousand good deeds and twenty-four thousand good deeds. A man said: How will we perish after this, O Messenger of God? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A man will come on the Day of Resurrection with deeds which, if placed on a mountain, would weigh it down. Then a blessing or God’s blessings will arise and it will almost exhaust them all, unless God covers him with His mercy. Then this Surah was revealed: “Has there not come over man a period of time…” until His saying: a great kingdom. The Abyssinian said: My eyes see what your eyes see in Paradise. He said: Yes. Then he wept until his soul departed. Ibn Umar said: “I saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) lowering him into his grave with his hand.” And His, the Most High, saying: Above them will be green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade. That is, the clothing of the people of Paradise therein will be silk, and from this comes fine brocade, such as shirts and the like, which are close to their bodies. Brocade is that which has luster and shine, and is close to the outer surface, as is customary in clothing. And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver. This is a description of the righteous. As for those brought near, as God Almighty said: They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their clothing therein will be silk. And when God Almighty mentioned the adornment of the outer surface with silk and jewelry, He said after that: And their Lord will give them to drink a pure drink. That is, He will purify their inner selves from envy, hatred, malice, harm, and all other bad morals, as we narrated from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he said: When the people of Paradise reach the gate of Paradise, they will find two springs there, and it is as if they were inspired to do so, so they drank from one of them, and God removed the harm in their bellies.
